title: Transport finite disjoint open partitions across a thickening
statement: Let $p:P^\prime\to P$ be a surjective closed immersion of schemes. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $(W_j)_{j\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ be pairwise disjoint opens of $P^\prime$ with union $P^\prime$. There are pairwise disjoint opens $(V_j)$ covering $P$ such that each inclusion $V_j\to P$ is finite, and for each j a surjective closed immersion $a_j:W_j\to V_j$ whose composite with the inclusion into P equals the inclusion of W_j followed by p. The assertion includes n=0.

proof.text: The map p is a universal homeomorphism. Apply the order isomorphism on opens induced by its underlying homeomorphism to define V_j. The isomorphism preserves arbitrary suprema, top, infima and bottom, so the V_j form a disjoint covering. The inverse image of V_j is W_j.

For each j, the complement of V_j is the union of V_k for k unequal to j: coverage proves one inclusion and disjointness the other. This union is open, so V_j is closed. Its open inclusion is a preimmersion with closed range, hence a closed immersion, and therefore finite.

Use the open-subscheme isomorphism W_j ≅ p^{-1}(V_j), followed by the restriction of p to V_j, as a_j. Restrictions preserve closed immersions. Surjectivity is checked by lifting a point of V_j under p. The restriction inclusion equation and the open-subscheme isomorphism inclusion equation prove the required composite equation. No component argument is needed for n=0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_open_partition_thickening_transport
    {P' P : Scheme.{u}} (p : P' ⟶ P) [IsClosedImmersion p] [Surjective p]
    (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → P'.Opens)
    (hcover : (⨆ j, W j) = ⊤)
    (hdisj : Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (W j) (W k))) :
    ∃ V : Fin n → P.Opens,
      (⨆ j, V j) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (V j) (V k)) ∧
      ∀ j, IsFinite (V j).ι ∧
        ∃ a : (W j).toScheme ⟶ (V j).toScheme,
          IsClosedImmersion a ∧ Surjective a ∧ a ≫ (V j).ι = (W j).ι ≫ p
